I read only the anonymous packet and its approved notation context. I did not consult a source, declaration identity, or other repository files. The packet reports `compiled: true`; I did not independently run Lean.

The following is the complete reconstructed mathematical statement.

Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, equipped with its normed additive-group structure and its Borel measurable-space structure. Let \(V:E\to\mathbb R\), and let \(\kappa\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}\). Assume
\[
1\le\kappa,\qquad V\in C^2(E;\mathbb R),
\]
and, for every \(x,w\in E\),
\[
\kappa^{-1}\|w\|^2
\le D^2V(x)[w,w]\le \|w\|^2.
\]
Assume the real dimension
\[
d=\dim_{\mathbb R}E
\]
is strictly positive. In formulas below, \(d\) denotes this dimension cast to a real number, and nonnegative-real state coordinates and \(\kappa\) are likewise cast to reals where needed.

The state space is
\[
S=\mathbb R_{\ge0}\times E\times E\times\mathbb N\times E^{\mathbb N}.
\]
Write a state as \(s=(b,a,x,k,h)\), where \(h:\mathbb N\to E\) is a full infinite sequence. Let \(\eta:S\to\mathbb R\) be measurable. Let \(c,\Delta\in\mathbb R\) satisfy
\[
0<c<\tfrac14,\qquad
\forall s\in S,\quad 0<\eta(s)\le c,\qquad
0<\Delta\le\tfrac12.
\]
Fix any initial state \(s_0=(b_0,a_0,x_0,k_0,h_0)\), without further restrictions, and any Markov kernel \(M:S\rightsquigarrow E\). In particular, no approximation-quality, absolute-continuity, or finite-relative-entropy assumption is imposed on \(M\).

Define
\[
K(r)=\frac{1+r}{\kappa^{-1}+r},
\qquad
\tau(s)=
\begin{cases}
K(b),&2\le K(b),\\
c,&K(b)<2,
\end{cases}
\]
and
\[
L=2+\log\!\left(\frac{2K(b_0)d}{\Delta}\right),\qquad
B=\frac{1/1024}{\sqrt{dL}+L},
\]
\[
J=\left\lceil 8\log\!\left(\frac{eK(b_0)}B\right)\right\rceil_{\mathbb N},
\qquad
\varepsilon=\frac{\Delta}{\sqrt{J+1}}.
\]
The displayed natural ceiling is the total natural-number ceiling operation. The local name \(\varepsilon\) does not occur subsequently in the formal conclusion.

For each \(s=(b,a,x,k,h)\), define
\[
v(s)=\frac{\eta(s)+\tau(s)}{1+b},\qquad
b^+(s)=b+\operatorname{toNNReal}\!\left(v(s)^{-1}\right).
\]
Here \(\operatorname{toNNReal}\) truncates below at zero. Keep this operation as displayed rather than silently replacing it in the formal specification.

For \(p=(s,(y,z))\in S\times(E\times E)\), define
\[
o(p)=y+\sqrt{\frac{\tau(s)}{1+b}}\,z,
\]
\[
a^+(p)=b^+(s)^{-1}\bigl(ba+v(s)^{-1}o(p)\bigr),
\]
\[
F_p(u)=V(u)+\frac{b^+(s)}2\|u-a^+(p)\|^2,
\qquad
T_p(u)=u-\frac{1}{1+b^+(s)}\nabla F_p(u).
\]
Inverses involving \(b^+(s)\) above use its real coercion. Set
\[
q_n(p)=\left\|\nabla F_p\!\left(T_p^{\,n}(y)\right)\right\|^2
\]
and define the total first-hit index
\[
N(p)=
\begin{cases}
\min\{n\in\mathbb N:q_n(p)\le(\kappa^{-1}+b^+(s))d\},
&\text{if this set is nonempty},\\
0,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
Define the state update
\[
U(p)=\bigl(b^+(s),\,a^+(p),\,T_p^{\,N(p)}(y),\,k+1,\,h^+(p)\bigr),
\]
where
\[
h^+(p)(0)=o(p),\qquad h^+(p)(n+1)=h(n).
\]
Thus this iteration starts at the newly sampled \(y\), not at the third coordinate \(x\) of the incoming state.

The terminal construction uses, for each state \(s=(b,a,x,k,h)\),
\[
\bar b(s)=\max\{b,B^{-1}\},
\]
\[
F_s^{\mathrm t}(u)=V(u)+\frac{\bar b(s)}2\|u-a\|^2,
\qquad
T_s^{\mathrm t}(u)=u-\frac{1}{1+\bar b(s)}\nabla F_s^{\mathrm t}(u),
\]
\[
q_n^{\mathrm t}(s)
=\left\|\nabla F_s^{\mathrm t}\!\left((T_s^{\mathrm t})^n(x)\right)\right\|^2,
\]
\[
N^{\mathrm t}(s)=
\begin{cases}
\min\{n\in\mathbb N:q_n^{\mathrm t}(s)\le d\bar b(s)\},
&\text{if this set is nonempty},\\
0,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
Then set
\[
x^{\mathrm t}(s)=(T_s^{\mathrm t})^{N^{\mathrm t}(s)}(x),
\quad
A(s)=\bar b(s)^{-1},
\quad
g(s)=\nabla V(x^{\mathrm t}(s)),
\quad
\theta(s)=a-A(s)g(s).
\]
This terminal iteration starts at the third state coordinate \(x\).

Let \(\gamma_E\) denote standard Gaussian measure on \(E\), and let
\[
\nu=\bigl(\mathrm{Leb}_{\mathbb R}|_{(0,1]}\bigr)\otimes\gamma_E.
\]
For a candidate \(y\in E\) and an auxiliary pair \((t,z_0)\in\mathbb R\times E\), put \(z=\sqrt{A(s)}\,z_0\) and define
\[
\begin{split}
W_s(y,(t,z_0))
=\min\Biggl\{1,\max\Biggl\{-1,\,
\Biggl\langle&
\frac{\pi}{2}\left(
\cos\!\left(\frac{\pi t}{2}\right)(y-\theta(s))
-\sin\!\left(\frac{\pi t}{2}\right)z
\right),\\
&g(s)-\nabla V\!\left(
\theta(s)
+\sin\!\left(\frac{\pi t}{2}\right)(y-\theta(s))
+\cos\!\left(\frac{\pi t}{2}\right)z
\right)
\Biggr\rangle_{\mathbb R}
\Biggr\}\Biggr\}.
\end{split}
\]
The expression is explicitly clipped to \([-1,1]\).

Define the candidate law
\[
R_s=(z\mapsto\theta(s)+\sqrt{A(s)}\,z)_\#\gamma_E.
\]
One trial is a tuple
\[
p=(Y,N,((T_i,Z_i))_{i\in\mathbb N},U)
\]
with independent coordinates distributed according to
\[
R_s\otimes
\left(
\operatorname{Poisson}(2)\otimes
\left(\nu^{\otimes\mathbb N}
\otimes(\mathrm{Leb}_{\mathbb R}|_{[0,1]})\right)
\right).
\]
The tuple grouping in this expression is the grouping of the displayed nested products. Let \(\rho_s\) be the independent countable product of this trial law. Thus \(\omega\) is an infinite sequence of independent trials.

Declare a trial accepted exactly when
\[
U\le
\prod_{i=0}^{N-1}\frac{1+W_s(Y,(T_i,Z_i))}{2}.
\]
The product is \(1\) for \(N=0\). Define the total output function
\[
\mathcal A_s(\omega)=
\begin{cases}
Y_{n_*},&
n_*=\min\{n\in\mathbb N:\omega_n\text{ is accepted}\}
\text{ exists},\\
0_E,&\text{if no trial is accepted}.
\end{cases}
\]

A further local measure is defined in the statement:
\[
\pi_s^{\mathrm t}
=
\left((z\mapsto a+\sqrt{A(s)}z)_\#\gamma_E\right)
.\operatorname{tilted}(-V).
\]
This local measure is unused in the asserted conclusion; in particular, there is no displayed assertion identifying the terminal output law with \(\pi_s^{\mathrm t}\).

Let
\[
\mu_V=\mathrm{Leb}_E.\operatorname{tilted}(-V),
\]
where `tilted` is the given total normalized exponential-reweighting operation.

The theorem concludes that \(\mu_V\) is a probability measure and that there exist Markov kernels
\[
L_{\mathrm t}:S\rightsquigarrow E,\qquad
P:S\rightsquigarrow S,\qquad
TG:S\rightsquigarrow E,\qquad
H:S\rightsquigarrow E
\]
with all of the following properties.

For every state \(s=(b,a,x,k,h)\),
\[
P(s)=
\begin{cases}
\delta_s,&B^{-1}\le b,\\
U(s,\cdot)_\#\bigl(M(s)\otimes\gamma_E\bigr),&b<B^{-1}.
\end{cases}
\]
The Gaussian used here is independent of the draw \(y\sim M(s)\). Above the threshold the entire state is fixed, including its counter and history sequence.

For every state \(s\),
\[
L_{\mathrm t}(s)=(\mathcal A_s)_\#\rho_s,
\]
\[
TG(s)=
\mu_V.\operatorname{tilted}
\left(u\mapsto-\frac b2\|u-a\|^2\right),
\]
and
\[
H(s)=
(u,w\mapsto u+w)_\#
\left[
TG(s)\otimes
(z\mapsto\sqrt{v(s)}z)_\#\gamma_E
\right].
\]

Define
\[
Q(s)=
(u,w\mapsto u+w)_\#
\left[
M(s)\otimes
\left(z\mapsto
\sqrt{\frac{\tau(s)}{1+b}}z\right)_\#\gamma_E
\right]
\]
and the extended-nonnegative error
\[
e(s)=
\begin{cases}
0,&B^{-1}\le b,\\
\operatorname{KL}(Q(s)\|H(s)),&b<B^{-1}.
\end{cases}
\]
The theorem asserts that \(e\) is measurable and, for every \(m\in\mathbb N\),
\[
\boxed{
\operatorname{KL}
\left(
(L_{\mathrm t}\circ P^{\,J+m})(s_0)
\,\middle\|\,TG(s_0)
\right)
\le
\sum_{j=0}^{J-1}
\int_S^{-}e(s)\,d(P^j(s_0))(s)
+
\operatorname{ofReal}_{\mathbb R_{\ge0}\cup\{\infty\}}
\left(\frac{\Delta^2}{J+1}\right).
}
\]
Here composition means first applying \(P^{J+m}\), then \(L_{\mathrm t}\). Kernel exponent zero is the identity kernel, so \(P^0(s_0)=\delta_{s_0}\). The target on the left is the measure \(TG(s_0)\) at the original initial state. The sum on the right stops at \(J-1\), independently of \(m\).

All KL divergences and displayed nonnegative integrals take values in the extended nonnegative reals. The assertion includes the possibility of infinite KL or an infinite right-hand side; it contains no implicit finiteness or absolute-continuity hypothesis. When the right-hand side is finite, the inequality bounds the final KL by that finite quantity; when it is infinite, the displayed inequality remains an extended-real assertion.

The statement retains three explicit fallback branches: the ordinary gradient-iteration first hit defaults to \(0\) if absent, the terminal gradient-iteration first hit defaults to \(0\) if absent, and the repeated-trial output defaults to \(0_E\) if there is no accepted trial. There is no separate displayed termination-probability, iteration-count, expected-cost, or runtime bound. The existence of the asserted Markov kernels includes probability of their fibers, but the text does not separately assert that these fallback events are null.

The constants \(L,B,J\) depend on \(\kappa,d,b_0,\Delta\); \(\tau\) also uses \(c\), and \(v\) uses \(\eta\). The transition kernel can depend on every state coordinate through arbitrary measurable \(\eta\) and \(M\), including the full history sequence and counter. No finite-memory restriction is imposed.
